Europe Under-18 Championship|2013 Latvia]]|[[Spain national under-18 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Juan Alberto''' "'''Juancho'''" '''Hernangómez Geuer''' (born 28 September 1995) is a Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] with the 15th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA Draft|2016 NBA draft]] and spent seven seasons in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] before returning to [[Europe]]. He is an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection and won the EuroLeague in [[2023–24 EuroLeague|2024]]. Hernangómez represents the senior [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spanish national team]] in international competition.{{cite web |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Juan-Alberto-Hernangomez/Summary/52816 |title=Juancho Hernangomez Player Profile |work=RealGM.com |access-date=9 March 2016}} He won the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] and played a crucial part in winning the [[EuroBasket 2022]], scoring a game-high 27 points in the final against France.{{cite web |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2022/09/18/behind-27-from-juancho-hernangomez-spain-knocks-off-france-to-win-eurobasket-title/ |title=Behind 27 from Juancho Hernangomez, Spain knocks off France to win EuroBasket title |date=18 September 2022}} Additionally to his playing career, Hernangómez co-starred in the [[Netflix]] basketball film ''[[Hustle (2022 film)|Hustle]]'' in 2022, alongside [[Adam Sandler]]. ==Early career== Hernangómez began playing competitive basketball in 2007, with the youth teams of [[CB Las Rozas]]. He joined a youth squad of [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] and played with the team until moving to Club Baloncesto Majadahonda for the following years.{{cite web |title=Juancho Hernangómez |url=http://clubestudiantes.com/frontend/clubestudiantes/noticia.php?id_noticia=10278&id_seccion=449 |work=ClubEstudiantes.com |access-date=9 March 2016}} ==Professional career== === CB Estudiantes (2012–2016) === [[File:Juan Hernangomez.jpg|thumb|right|Hernangómez with [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]] in 2013]] In 2012 Hernangómez signed his first professional contract with [[CB Estudiantes]] and played with the club's reserve side until 2014, when he was promoted to the first team.{{cite web |url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Juancho_Hernangomez/Spain/Tuenti_Movil_Estudiantes_Madrid/250378 |title=Juancho Hernangomez basketball profile |work=Eurobasket.com |access-date=2016-03-09}} In the 2015–16 ACB season Hernangómez averaged 9.7 points and 5.7 rebounds across 34 games and was named the [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB Best Young Player]].{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/199751/juancho-hernangomez-named-best-young-player-of-acb-season.html |title=Juancho Hernangomez named best young player of ACB season |work=Sportando.com |date=2016-05-18 |access-date=2016-05-18}} ===Denver Nuggets (2016–2020)=== [[File:Juan Hernangómez 2020.jpg|thumb|right|Hernangómez with the [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2020]] On 26 April 2016, Hernangómez was named in the international early entry candidates list for the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/NBA-Announced-Early-Entry-Candidates-for-2016-NBA-Draft-5460/ |title=NBA Announced Early Entry Candidates for 2016 NBA Draft |work=DraftExpress.com |date=6 April 2016 |access-date=6 April 2016 |archive-date=30 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160430035516/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/NBA-Announced-Early-Entry-Candidates-for-2016-NBA-Draft-5460/ |url-status=dead }} He was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] with the 15th overall pick.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-select-murray-hernangomez-beasley-2016-nba-draft/ |title=Denver Nuggets Select Murray, Hernangomez and Beasley in First Round of 2016 NBA Draft |work=NBA.com |date=24 June 2016 |access-date=24 June 2016}} On 9 August 2016, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Nuggets.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-murray-hernangomez-beasley-080916 |title=Nuggets Sign Murray, Hernangomez and Beasley |work=NBA.com |date=9 August 2016 |access-date=9 August 2016}} On 4 January 2017, he was assigned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]], pursuant to the flexible assignment rule.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-assign-beasley-hernangomez-sioux-falls-skyforce-010417 |title=Denver Nuggets Assign Malik Beasley and Juancho Hernangomez to Sioux Falls Skyforce |work=NBA.com |date=4 January 2017 |access-date=4 January 2017}} He was recalled by the Nuggets three days later after appearing in one game for the Skyforce.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-recall-juancho-hernangomez-010717 |title=Denver Nuggets Recall Juancho Hernangomez |work=NBA.com |date=7 January 2017 |access-date=7 January 2017}} On 13 February 2017, he scored a season-high 27 points to go with a season-best 10 rebounds in a 132–110 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He hit six three-pointers against the Warriors to help the Nuggets tie an NBA record with 24 three-pointers.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900232 |title=Nuggets tie NBA mark with 24 3s in 132-110 win over Warriors |work=ESPN.com |date=13 February 2017 |access-date=14 February 2017}} Early in the 2017–18 season, Hernangomez was diagnosed with mononucleosis,{{Cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/10/24/nuggets-juancho-hernangomez-mononucleosis |title=Denver Nuggets' Juancho Hernangomez out with ==mononucleosis== {{!}} NBA.com|work=NBA.com|access-date=15 August 2018|language=en}} and as a result, he played in only 25 games during his sophomore campaign. ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2020–2021)=== On 5 February 2020, Hernangómez was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Brooklyn Nets' 2020 First Round Pick from Atlanta Hawks, Malik Beasley, Juancho Hernangomez and Jarred Vanderbilt from Denver Nuggets in 12-Player, Four-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-brooklyn-nets-2020-first-round-pick-atlanta-hawks-malik-beasley |website=NBA.com |access-date=6 February 2020 |date=5 February 2020}} He re-signed with the Timberwolves on a three-year deal on 27 November 2020. The 2020–21 season was a tumultuous one for Hernangómez as he showed up to training camp out of shape, contracted COVID-19, and lost his spot in the starting lineup, capped off by a falling out with the Timberwolves front office over their decision to disallow him from participating in the 2021 Olympics after suffering a shoulder injury during an exhibition game.{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2726973/2021/07/24/sources-juancho-hernangomez-angered-after-wolves-block-him-from-olympics/ |title=Sources: Juancho Hernangomez angered after Wolves block him from Olympics |website=[[The Athletic]] |last1=Krawczynski |first1=Jon}} === Boston Celtics (2021–2022) === On 25 August 2021, Hernangómez and [[Jarrett Culver]] were traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Patrick Beverley]]{{cite web |title=Grizzlies acquire Jarrett Culver and Juancho Hernangomez from Timberwolves |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-jarrett-culver-and-juancho-hernangomez-from-timberwolves-210825 |website=NBA.com |date=25 August 2021 |access-date=25 August 2021}} and on 15 September, he was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Kris Dunn]], [[Carsen Edwards]] and the right for a 2026 second-round pick swap.{{cite web |title=Celtics Acquire Juancho Hernangómez in Three-Player Trade with Grizzlies |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-juancho-hernangomez-three-player-trade-grizzlies |website=NBA.com |date=15 September 2021 |access-date=15 September 2021}} === San Antonio Spurs (2022) === On 19 January 2022, Hernangómez was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Denver Nuggets]], sending [[Bol Bol]] and [[PJ Dozier]] to Boston and [[Bryn Forbes]] to Denver.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-acquire-juancho-hernangomez-second-round-pick |title=SPURS ACQUIRE JUANCHO HERNANGÓMEZ & SECOND ROUND PICK |work=NBA.com |date=19 January 2022}} === Utah Jazz (2022) === On 9 February 2022, Hernangómez was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in a three-team trade.{{Cite web |title=Jazz Acquire Alexander-Walker and Hernangomez |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-acquire-alexander-walker-and-hernangomez |access-date=9 February 2022 |website=NBA}} On 30 June, he was waived by the Jazz.{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz waive Juancho Hernangomez, as roster reshaping continues |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2022/06/30/jazz-waive-juancho-hernangomez/ |access-date=30 June 2022 |website=The Salt Lake Tribune}} === Toronto Raptors (2022–2023) === On 27 July 2022, Hernangómez signed a one-year contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]] for an amount equal to the veteran's minimum.{{cite web |title=Raptors sign Juancho Hernangomez |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-hernangomez |website=NBA.com |date=28 July 2022 |access-date=19 August 2025}} During the 2022–23 [[NBA season|season]], he found himself out of the team's rotation and was a healthy scratch in several games.{{cite web |title=Raptors waive Juancho Hernangomez |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/02/28/raptors-waive-juancho-hernangomez-hustle-will-barton |website=SI.com |date=28 February 2023 |access-date=19 August 2025}} On 28 February 2023, the [[Toronto Raptors|Raptors]] waived Hernangómez to make room for guard [[Will Barton]].{{cite web |title=Raptors sign guard Will Barton, waive Juancho Hernangomez |url=https://www.nba.com/news/raptors-sign-guard-will-barton-waive-juancho-hernangomez |website=NBA.com |date=28 February 2023 |access-date=19 August 2025}} Reflecting on his time with the Raptors, Hernangómez expressed surprise at being waived, noting, "It surprised me when they waived me because I was really good in the locker room, good teammate and working hard every single day."{{cite web |title=Juancho Hernangómez: Why he doesn't like being called “Bo Cruz” |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/interviews/1561177/juancho-hernangomez-why-he-doesnt-like-being-called-bo-cruz-choosing-panathinaikos-over-barcelona-hurtful-nba-exit/ |website=Eurohoops.net |date=19 August 2025 |access-date=19 August 2025}} === Panathinaikos (2023–present) === On 27 July 2023, Hernangómez signed a two-year, 4,500,000€ deal with [[EuroLeague]] powerhouse [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], returning to European basketball after seven years.{{cite web |title=Στον Παναθηναϊκό ο Χουάντσο Ερνανγκόμεθ |url=https://www.paobc.gr/deltia-typoy/104010_ston-panathinaiko-o-hoyantso-ernangkometh |website=PaoBC.gr |date=27 July 2023 |access-date=27 July 2023 |language=Greek}} On 19 July 2023, Hernangómez signed a two–year contract with Greek club [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].{{cite web |title=Panathinaikos officially signs Juancho Hernangomez |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1524050/panathinaikos-officially-signs-juancho-hernangomez/ |website=Eurohoops |date=19 July 2023 |access-date=19 August 2025}} His first season in Athens was considered underwhelming, with head coach [[Ergin Ataman]] publicly critical of his performances.{{cite web |title=Juancho Hernangómez encuentra su sitio en el Panathinaikos |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/baloncesto/2025-03-06/juancho-hernangomez-encuentra-su-sitio-en-el-panathinaikos.html |website=El País |date=6 March 2025 |language=es |access-date=19 August 2025}} However, Hernangómez found improved form in his second year, becoming an important part of the team’s rotation. On January 3, 2025, Panathinaikos announced that Hernangómez had extended his contract until 2027.{{cite web |title=Panathinaikos officially re-signs Juancho Hernangomez until 2027 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1766056/panathinaikos-officially-re-signs-juancho-hernangomez-until-2027/ |website=Eurohoops |date=10 January 2025 |access-date=19 August 2025}} Hernangómez’s standout moment came during the [[2025 EuroLeague Playoffs]], when he was named MVP of Game 1 against Anadolu Efes after a dominant all-around performance.{{cite web |title=Juancho Hernangomez MVP of EuroLeague Playoffs Game 1 |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/euroleague-playoffs-game-1-mvp-juancho-hernangomez/ |website=Sportando |date=23 April 2025 |access-date=19 August 2025}}{{cite web |title=Juancho Hernangomez historic game in Panathinaikos win over Efes |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1815063/juancho-hernangomez-panathinaikos-anadolu-efes-euroleague-playoffs-game-1-post-game-interviews/ |website=Eurohoops |date=23 April 2025 |access-date=19 August 2025}} His performances throughout the season earned him a place in the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]].{{cite web |title=2024–25 All-EuroLeague Teams announced |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/news/2025/all-euroleague-teams-announced-2025/ |website=EuroLeague |date=May 2025 |access-date=19 August 2025}} Spanish daily ''AS'' described him as having finally "let loose" in the Panathinaikos jersey after a difficult start.{{cite web |title=Juancho se desmelena |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/euroliga/juancho-se-desmelena-n/ |website=AS |date=24 April 2025 |language=es |access-date=19 August 2025}} ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== In 2013, Hernangómez competed with the [[Spain national under-18 basketball team]] at the [[FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] in [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|Latvia]]. He joined the [[Spain national under-18 basketball team|under-20 team]] for the following two years, playing at the [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]]. Hernangómez also helped the [[Spain men's national basketball team|senior Spain national team]] practice for the [[EuroBasket 2015]].{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/national-teams/national-teams/173992/juancho-hernangomez-and-alberto-abalde-to-help-spanish-nt-at-practices.html |title=Juancho Hernangomez and Alberto Abalde to help Spanish NT at practices |work=Sportando |date=26 August 2015 |access-date=9 March 2016}} ===Senior national team=== His senior Spain national team major tournament debut was at the [[EuroBasket 2017]]. Hernangomez averaged 8.4 points, 5.9 rebounds, 0.7 assists and 0.7 blocked shots in 19.7 minutes per game.{{Cite web |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/player/Juan-Hernangomez |title=Juan Hernangomez at the FIBA EuroBasket 2017 - FIBA.basketball |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en |access-date=15 August 2018}} Spain finished in third place, winning the bronze medal.{{Cite web |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/news/spain-win-bronze-to-send-navarro-off-in-style |title=Spain win Bronze to send Navarro off in style |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en |access-date=15 August 2018}} In June 2018, Hernangomez was again named to the Spain national team's roster in advance of the first stage of qualifiers for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2018/06/20/juancho-hernangomez-spanish-national-team/ |title=Denver Nuggets' Juancho Hernangomez named to Spain national team roster |date=20 June 2018 |work=The Denver Post |access-date=15 August 2018 |language=en-US}} Hernangómez and Spain won a surprising gold medal at [[EuroBasket 2022]]. In the [[EuroBasket 2022 Final|final]] against [[France men's national basketball team|France]], Hernangómez scored 27 points including seven three-pointers to guide Spain to a convincing win.{{Cite web |date=18 September 2022 |title=Spain claim FIBA EuroBasket 2022 crown |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/news/spain-claim-fiba-eurobasket-2022-crown |access-date=2022-09-19 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} He was third on the team in scoring (12.8 points per game) and third in rebounding as well (5.0 per game).{{Cite web |title=Spain at the FIBA EuroBasket 2022 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/team/Spain |access-date=2022-09-19 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} His brother [[Willy Hernangómez|Willy]] was also on the team and won Hernangomez brothers - watch this space! |work=FIBA.com |date=26 July 2015 |access-date=9 March 2016}} ==Acting career== In 2022, Hernangómez made his acting debut in the Netflix sports drama film ''[[Hustle (2022 film)|Hustle]]'', produced by [[Adam Sandler]]’s Happy Madison Productions and [[LeBron James]]’ SpringHill Company.{{cite web |title=Netflix's Hustle Review: Adam Sandler Shines in Basketball Drama |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2022/jun/03/hustle-review-adam-sandler-netflix |website=The Guardian |date=3 June 2022 |access-date=19 August 2025}} He portrayed fictional Spanish prospect Bo Cruz, a gifted but troubled streetball player discovered by Sandler’s character, scout Stanley Sugerman. The film received positive reviews from critics, with Hernangómez’s performance being highlighted as natural and charismatic.{{cite web |title='Hustle' Review: Adam Sandler, Juancho Hernangómez, and a Slam Dunk of a Sports Movie |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/06/03/movies/hustle-review-adam-sandler.html |website=The New York Times |date=3 June 2022 |access-date=19 August 2025}} The role brought Hernangómez international recognition outside basketball, with media outlets noting his on-screen chemistry with Sandler and his convincing transition to acting.{{cite web |title=Juancho Hernangómez steals the show in Adam Sandler's Hustle |url=https://variety.com/2022/film/reviews/hustle-review-adam-sandler-1235281389/ |website=Variety |date=2 June 2022 |access-date=19 August 2025}} ==Family== Hernangómez's immediate family is made up of former or current basketball players. His older brother [[Willy Hernangómez|Willy]] currently plays for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]],{{cite web |title=Willy Hernangómez, culer fins al 2026 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.cat/ca/basquet/primer-equip/noticies/3587720/willy-hernangomez-culer-fins-al-2026 |website=FCBarcelona.cat |date=12 July 2023 |access-date=14 July 2023 |language=Catalan}} having previously played for the [[New Orleans Pelicans|Pelicans]], [[Charlotte Hornets|Hornets]], [[New York Knicks|Knicks]], and [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]. His mother [[Margarita Geuer|Margarita Geuer Draeger]] was an international basketball player, winning a European championship with Spain in [[EuroBasket Women 1993|1993]]. His father also played for Real Madrid and [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]] and his younger sister currently plays for Estudiantes' youth team. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *
